title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, server timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description: Context and motivation: Recent customers and internal canaries showed flaky streaming behavior when clients cancel, abruptly disconnect, or reconnect mid-stream. This manifests as leaked server-side resources (stalled KV caches), inconsistent stream resume semantics across SDKs, and rare cases where server-side timeouts close flows before clients can reconnect. This PR implements deterministic lifecycle controls for streaming: 1) explicit client-cancel handling with immediate server-side work cancellation and resource cleanup; 2) graceful disconnect handling that preserves resumable state for a configurable window; 3) reconnect/resume protocol (resume token + offset) compatible with Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer; 4) server-side idle/processing timeouts with configurable thresholds and clear error semantics so clients can decide retry vs resume. Changes in this PR touch the runtime request lifecycle, the gateway handler, the OpenAI-compat compatibility layer, and SDK-facing contract docs. Summary of changes: - Add StreamLifecycleManager component (runtime) to track active streams, KV-cache pinning, and cleanup hooks. - Introduce resumable_stream token metadata returned on stream start when the model/runtime supports resume. Token includes compact epoch/offset and HMAC to prevent tampering. - On client-cancel: handler now emits a Cancellation signal that triggers immediate tokenized cancel, flush of per-request buffers, and release of any pinned resources; returns a 200-stream-closed event to client. - On disconnect: runtime marks stream as disconnected and keeps resume state for resume_window (default 90s). Background sweeper enforces the resume_window and triggers cleanup. - Reconnect flow: client supplies resume_token; gateway validates HMAC, checks epoch/offset compatibility, and issues ResumeAccepted or ResumeRejected with reason (stale_token, offset_mismatch). - Server timeouts: split idle_timeout (no client activity) and processing_timeout (server-side stalled ops); explicit error types STREAM_TIMEOUT_IDLE and STREAM_TIMEOUT_PROCESSING are emitted to clients and logged with trace IDs. - OpenAI-compat: extend existing /v1/streams behavior to include the resume protocol as opt-in via header X-Redwood-Resume: true; maintain backward compatibility if absent. - Add tests: unit tests for manager, end-to-end integration tests simulating disconnect/reconnect, and canary test harness update. - Docs: API contract, SDK notes for Python/TS, migration guidance and rollback plan. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for clients that do not opt-in to resume; cancel/disconnect semantics improved but do not change HTTP status codes except when resume is attempted and rejected (returns 409 conflict with structured error). Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag (runtime flag + gateway config) with canary on production region us-west-2; monitor metrics (stream_reconnect_success, stream_resume_rejected, pinned_kv_count, stream_cleanup_latency). Observability: add tracing spans for lifecycle transitions and new metrics; tie alerts to stream_cleanup_latency and resume_reject_rate. Test plan: unit tests (runtime manager edge cases), integration harness with simulated network drops, load test to validate cleanup under 10k concurrent streams, SDK examples. Risks and mitigations: resume tokens add state - mitigated by short default resume_window and HMAC protection; mismatched offsets may confuse clients - we return structured error with recommended client action. Release notes: - Streaming: add optional resumable streaming protocol (X-Redwood-Resume header) with client-cancel/disconnect/reconnect lifecycle controls and clearer timeout semantics. See docs for migration.

review_comments: Samir Rao (2026-02-17): Overall design looks good. Two requests: (1) please add a short-lived HMAC on resume_token and validate in gateway (to avoid token forgery); (2) ensure we have a clear metric for pinned_kv_count so we can alert on leaks.
Asha Patel (2026-02-17): Added HMAC and validation; expose pinned_kv_count metric and unit tests to assert KV unpin on cancel. PTAL.

Evelyn Chen (2026-02-19): Can we avoid changing default flow for existing clients? Confirmed opt-in header is only required for resume; we should document exact HTTP semantics returned on resume rejection.
Asha Patel (2026-02-20): Confirmed default flow unchanged; added structured 409 response with fields error.code, error.reason, error.suggested_action in docs and gateway.

Derek Wallace (2026-02-22): Load test shows cleanup latency spike under 8k+ concurrent disconnects. Recommend increasing sweeper parallelism and adding backpressure on new streams when pinned_kv_count > threshold.
Asha Patel (2026-02-24): Implemented sweeper concurrency and backpressure config; added canary to rollout plan and load tests updated.

merge_commit_message: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect; add resume protocol and server timeouts
release_notes: Streaming: optional resumable streams (X-Redwood-Resume), deterministic client-cancel handling, disconnect/resume semantics, and explicit server timeouts (STREAM_TIMEOUT_IDLE, STREAM_TIMEOUT_PROCESSING). Backwards compatible unless resume is used.
migration_guidance: Clients who want resume must opt-in with header X-Redwood-Resume: true and implement resume token storage. If resume is not used, no change required. On resume rejection, prefer a fresh request rather than retrying with the same token. SDKs updated with helper utilities.
observability_changes: Added metrics: stream_reconnect_success, stream_resume_rejected, pinned_kv_count, stream_cleanup_latency. Added tracing spans: StreamLifecycle:Start, :Disconnect, :ResumeAttempt, :Cancelled, :Cleanup.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Phase 1: enable in canary (us-west-2) for ten percent of traffic for 72h. Phase 2: monitor metrics and expand to 50% for next 48h. Phase 3: global enable. Immediate rollback by disabling runtime flag and gateway header acceptance.
tests_summary: Unit tests cover lifecycle manager edge cases. Integration tests simulate client disconnect/reconnect with offset mismatches and stale tokens. Load tests validate cleanup under 10k concurrent streams; initial run revealed sweep latency issue that was addressed.
notes: Related Linear tickets: ENG-1842 (streaming reliability), ENG-1899 (openai-compat resume). Hotfixes required for an earlier incident were cherry-picked into release branch. No breaking change to existing clients unless resume is used.
authors_followup_actions: Monitor stream_cleanup_latency and resume_reject_rate dashboards for 72h after rollout; coordinate SDK patch releases for Python/TS to expose resume helpers.
